reason: Hotel disruptions were removed from the airline-only product scope. Records are preserved for provenance and possible reinstatement and are not loaded at runtime.

cases.facts: Guest booked a Holiday Inn in Boston through Chase Sapphire Preferred and later noticed a security deposit charge that appeared incorrect. The guest considered a card dispute before contacting the hotel.
requested_compensation: Refund of incorrect security deposit charge
Written folio or explanation of the charge
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported beyond forum advice. Other users recommended contacting or emailing the hotel first because the charge might be a billing error or pending adjustment.
cases.reusable_lesson: For unexplained hotel charges, request the folio and a written billing correction from the property before escalating to a card dispute.
cases.notes: Summarized and rewritten from a USCardForum '怎么撕？' tagged thread.
review_notes: Outcome is incomplete; do not use as a compensation benchmark.

cases.facts: Hyatt Regency Maui notified guests that the Regency Club would be closed during a renovation period. The property offered daily breakfast at another restaurant for Globalists and options for guests using club-related awards, such as keeping breakfast access or having an award returned.
requested_compensation: Return of club access or Guest of Honor award if preferred
Possible goodwill if evening club value was important
cases.actual_outcome: Forum consensus was that restaurant breakfast was a reasonable or even favorable substitute for this property, and additional compensation beyond the stated options was uncertain.
evidence_used: Reservation showing club access or elite status
Terms of the award or elite benefit
cases.reusable_lesson: For temporary club lounge closures, compare the substitute breakfast and award-return options against the lost benefit. Stronger asks need evidence that the closure materially reduced the booked benefit.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic read via Nitan.

cases.facts: Marriott Platinum member staying at Renaissance New York Times Square was denied breakfast benefit. The hotel offered only 1,000 points or two cookies as breakfast alternative, while a full hot breakfast cost $57 per person plus tax and tip. The hotel charged $7 for Costco-style bottled water. Guest opened the Brilliant card specifically expecting the breakfast benefit.
requested_compensation: Proper breakfast benefit as per Marriott Platinum policy
Points compensation for denied elite benefit
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported in the captured thread. The guest appeared resigned to not getting the breakfast benefit at this property.
cases.reusable_lesson: Not all Marriott properties honor elite breakfast benefits consistently. Check property-specific policies on FlyerTalk before booking, and consider choosing properties with confirmed breakfast benefits for Platinum+ members.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Facts clear but outcome incomplete. Property may not participate in the breakfast benefit program.
review_notes: Outcome is incomplete; do not use as a compensation benchmark.

cases.facts: Guest staying at a Conrad property in China (Hangzhou/Tonglu area) using Hilton Aspire credits. At checkout, the guest took a 'water bottle' from the minibar area and drank from it — it was filled with dishwashing liquid (possibly a housekeeper's refill bottle that was mistakenly left). The guest immediately spat it out, rinsed for an hour, and felt nauseated all day. The hotel denied responsibility, claiming an 'internal investigation' found nothing. The guest also had a prior bad experience at the same hotel (denied a double-bed suite without upgrade). The guest initially demanded 100k points / 1 free night / 1 night refund from the hotel, then escalated to Hilton Diamond desk demanding 200k points / 2 free nights / 2 night refund.
requested_compensation: 100,000 Hilton points OR 1 free night certificate OR 1 night refund (to hotel)
Then escalated to 200,000 Hilton points OR 2 free nights OR 2 night refund (to Hilton Diamond desk)
cases.actual_outcome: Hotel refused compensation after a perfunctory internal investigation. Guest escalated to Hilton Diamond customer service desk but outcome was not reported in the captured thread.
evidence_used: Photo of the water bottle filled with dishwashing liquid showing pink/foamy residue
escalation_path: Hotel management → Hilton Diamond customer service (diamond@hrcc-hilton.com)
cases.reusable_lesson: Always check bottled water seals in hotel rooms — if the seal is broken, do not consume. Document contamination immediately with photos. If hotel denies responsibility, escalate to brand-level customer service. In China, local media (like 1818 Gold Eye) and food safety laws (1,000 RMB minimum) can be effective leverage.
cases.notes: Guest also had a prior Hilton Shanghai Hongqiao cockroach incident mentioned in the same escalation but not detailed here. The water bottle appeared to be a housekeeper's refill container mistakenly left in the room.
review_notes: Possible chemical ingestion is a health/safety case requiring professional help, outside the product boundary.

cases.facts: Guest brought personal towels to a Hyatt stay and housekeeping appears to have removed them with hotel linens. The front desk initially offered a hotel towel rather than finding or reimbursing the personal item.
requested_compensation: Return of personal item if recoverable
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported in the captured thread. Forum advice suggested deciding the desired remedy first, then asking the manager or Hyatt customer care for item replacement or points.
evidence_used: Description or receipt for personal item
escalation_path: Credit card purchase protection if eligible
cases.reusable_lesson: For minor personal-property loss at a hotel, anchor the request on replacement value and documentation, while treating points or fee adjustment as goodwill.
cases.notes: Summarized and rewritten from a USCardForum '怎么撕？' tagged thread.
review_notes: Outcome is incomplete; do not use as a compensation benchmark.

cases.facts: The new Hyatt Regency Rome Central (Cat 4) repeatedly delayed its opening from January to September. Initially, Hyatt offered to cancel and refund points or arrange comparable hotel accommodation. As Rome entered peak summer season with high hotel prices, Hyatt began relocating guests to a Hilton Garden Inn — a significantly lower-tier property. Forum discussion noted Hyatt has a JDV property in Rome (The RomeHello) that would be more comparable but was not being used.
requested_compensation: Return of points if substitute is lower value
Goodwill points for accepting a lower-tier substitute
cases.actual_outcome: Hyatt's relocation policy evolved from generous (cancel + comparable hotel) to less favorable (Hilton Garden Inn) as peak season arrived. Outcomes varied per guest; some were still waiting for relocation arrangements.
evidence_used: Cash rate comparison between original booking and substitute
cases.reusable_lesson: For pre-arrival hotel relocation due to delayed opening, proactively contact Hyatt concierge to discuss substitute options rather than waiting for a default assignment. If points were used, ask for them back if the substitute is materially lower quality.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Clear ongoing situation with multiple guest data points.
review_notes: Outcome is incomplete; do not use as a compensation benchmark.

cases.facts: Guest booked 4 nights base room at Conrad Bora Bora Nui with points. Paid $800/night to upgrade to overwater villa, confirmed via email one week before arrival. On the last day of a prior stay at St. Regis, received an email reverting the room to base. Hotel manager at check-in claimed no overwater villas were available despite the website showing availability. Offered a 'first two nights base, last two nights possible free upgrade' which was not guaranteed. Guest cancelled and booked Four Seasons at $11,000 for 4 nights instead.
requested_compensation: Compensation for breach of confirmed upgrade
cases.actual_outcome: Guest cancelled the reservation entirely and booked Four Seasons instead. Outcome of any refund or compensation claim not reported.
escalation_path: Credit card dispute for paid upgrade
cases.reusable_lesson: When a paid upgrade is confirmed in writing and then reneged, preserve all written confirmations and website availability screenshots. Cancelling the reservation may make compensation harder. Consider proceeding with the stay and disputing the upgrade charge afterward.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Very clear facts with written confirmation and documented bait-and-switch.
review_notes: Claim/refund outcome is not reported after the guest cancelled.

cases.facts: Guest booked Fairmont Banff Springs through Amex FHR. The assigned 'Gatehouse Queen' was presented as an upgrade, but the guest believed it was smaller than the booked room and lacked a desk. The guest documented the room, involved Amex Travel, and then escalated the disputed room description to the front desk manager.
cases.actual_outcome: Front desk manager handled it professionally: agreed to full refund of the entire stay, waived all extra charges including valet parking and dining not covered by FHR credit. Guest was satisfied with the resolution.
cases.reusable_lesson: Compare the confirmation and advertised room features with photos of the assigned room. Ask a manager and the booking channel to review the discrepancy, focusing on documented facts and the requested remedy rather than unsupported threats.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Very complete DP with clear outcome and actionable lessons.

cases.facts: Guest used points and suite upgrade benefits at Andaz 5th Avenue, then paid a nightly upgrade charge for a Wellness Suite mainly for the bathtub. The room allegedly lacked or had broken advertised amenities. Engineering could not fix one feature, and a promised points adjustment reportedly appeared incorrectly later.
requested_compensation: Refund or partial refund of paid upgrade charge
Points compensation for broken or missing advertised amenities
cases.actual_outcome: Partial outcome was discussed but not fully resolved in the captured thread.
evidence_used: Room type description or website screenshots
Photos of missing or broken amenities
cases.reusable_lesson: When paying for a specific room feature, document the advertised feature, the paid upgrade amount, and the defect while still on property. If points are promised in compensation, ask for the amount and case note in writing.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic.

cases.facts: Guest at a Hampton property ordered food through a QR code promoted in the hotel area, paid including tip, then learned the restaurant was closed and the order did not arrive. The front desk said it was unrelated to the hotel.
requested_compensation: Refund from restaurant or payment processor
Hotel goodwill points for poor on-property communication
Clarification whether the restaurant was hotel-affiliated
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported in the captured thread. Forum advice leaned toward disputing the undelivered food charge with the merchant/payment card and treating hotel compensation as goodwill only.
cases.reusable_lesson: Separate the refund claim against the food merchant from any goodwill request to the hotel, and document whether the restaurant was clearly presented as a hotel amenity.
cases.notes: Summarized and rewritten from a USCardForum '怎么撕？' tagged thread.
review_notes: Outcome is incomplete; do not use as a compensation benchmark.

cases.facts: Guest checked into an HGV property in Hawaii (Big Island) and found the wifi was completely non-functional in their double-bed room. An engineer tried to fix it without success. The manager said it was the only double-bed room available and could not upgrade to a 1BR/2BR suite, but offered a king room with a rollaway bed — which also had no working wifi. The guest returned to the original room. The manager offered compensation (points, resort fee waiver, or parking) but the guest felt it was trivial compared to the room cost. The next morning, the wifi was intermittent. The guest negotiated successfully.
requested_compensation: Compensation for unusable wifi (points / resort fee /)
cases.actual_outcome: After speaking to the manager the next morning, the hotel waived two nights of parking and resort fees plus applicable taxes, totaling approximately $190 USD. The guest considered this fair and did not pursue further compensation.
evidence_used: Demonstration of non-functional wifi to engineer and manager
escalation_path: Front desk engineer → Front desk manager
cases.reusable_lesson: Document the failed amenity and any attempted repair. In this case, asking a manager for specific fee waivers produced a mutually acceptable result; it does not establish a standard compensation amount.
cases.notes: Located in Hawaii (Big Island). The $190 in waived fees roughly matched the guest's on-property spending for the day.

cases.facts: Hilton Diamond member booked a Home2 Suites studio room for three people. At 4pm check-in, the system was down and only mobile key was available. The room lacked basic amenities for the confirmed occupancy: only one set of towels for three people, insufficient pillows, sheets, pillowcases, and blankets. Multiple requests to front desk from 4pm until 10:30pm resulted in no resolution — the property claimed sold out with no extra linens. No manager was on site. Hilton Diamond desk was closed.
requested_compensation: Reimbursement for additional expenses due to unusable accommodations
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported in the captured thread. Forum advice recommended contacting Hilton Diamond Desk or Guest Assistance to open a case against the property.
evidence_used: Timeline of requests to front desk
cases.reusable_lesson: When a property cannot provide basic accommodations for a confirmed booking, document every request and response in writing. Contact elite customer service directly rather than relying on the front desk.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Clear facts: confirmed booking, property failed to provide usable accommodations, no resolution after 6+ hours of requests.
review_notes: Reclassified from hotel_walk to hotel_service_issue; source outcome is not reported.

cases.facts: Booked 3 nights via Chase Travel (CSR) for $1,800. Multiple issues: bathroom ceiling panel fell off, sofa bed had stink bug corpse, unwashed sheets with dirt, live stink bug on wall. All issues photographed.
cases.actual_outcome: Front desk manager offered 1 night refund ($600). OP accepted. Hilton Twitter team facilitated resolution.
cases.reusable_lesson: Non-elite members can still get partial refunds for severe room issues. Document everything with photos. Twitter/X customer service often faster than phone. CSR booking provides extra support layer.
cases.notes: Multiple serious hygiene/safety issues documented. OP accepted 1-night refund without further push.

cases.facts: Guest booked 3 rooms for 3 nights via Agoda at Lyf Georgetown Penang (Ascott). At 1am on the last night, a false fire alarm sounded for ~30 seconds with flashing lights throughout the building. Guest's elderly mother was severely frightened and could not sleep afterward. Guest had to wake up at 5am for a flight. Guest requested a refund for the last night. Hotel refused, claiming they 'handled it well.' Agoda relayed the denial. Guest noted additional issues: AC water leaking onto furniture and a gecko in the bathroom.
requested_compensation: Compensation for distress caused to elderly guest
cases.actual_outcome: Hotel refused refund. Agoda relayed the decision. Guest was considering credit card chargeback but forum was divided on whether this was a valid dispute.
evidence_used: Photos of AC water leak and gecko
cases.reusable_lesson: For an OTA booking, document the issue while on property and contact both the hotel and booking channel. Separate the brief alarm from other documented service failures, and do not assume a card dispute is valid simply because a goodwill refund was denied.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. OTA booking complicates resolution. Forum consensus was that a false alarm alone is hard to claim compensation for.

cases.facts: Guest staying at a Hampton Inn on a free night award. A car accident broke a water main, causing the entire hotel to lose water from evening through the next day. No water for showering, flushing toilets, or breakfast. The hotel was also noisy overnight and in the early morning. Guest requested compensation for the unusable stay.
requested_compensation: Refund of the free night or points return
Compensation for loss of basic hotel services
cases.actual_outcome: At check-out, the front desk offered a refund. Since the booking was a free night certificate, they said they would ask Hilton about points compensation. Guest mentioned the maximum value of 80,000 points. Hilton was to decide on the amount.
evidence_used: Photos or documentation of water outage
cases.reusable_lesson: Report a loss of essential services while it is happening and keep the property's response. For an award booking, ask the loyalty program what form of refund or goodwill it can provide; the amount in this source remained unresolved.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Clear facts and reported partial outcome (refund offered, points compensation pending).

cases.facts: Guest staying at a Hyatt Centric in New York (40+ floors up). The fire alarm sounded — the first time, the hotel broadcasted that it was a false alarm from the rooftop bar and no evacuation was needed. The alarm stopped. Five minutes later, the alarm sounded again for 2-3 minutes with no further announcement. The guest decided to evacuate via the stairs (40+ floors down), encountering other confused guests doing the same. At the lobby, fire trucks had arrived, and the fire department was investigating. A hotel employee confirmed the alarm was cleared but only offered a casual apology. The guest felt the hotel's communication during a safety incident was dangerously inadequate.
requested_compensation: Compensation for stress and safety concern (guest was asking if it was worth pursuing)
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported in the captured thread. Commenters advised writing a complaint to Hyatt corporate citing safety concerns, with one reporting a prior successful claim of 25,000 points for a similar issue at another hotel.
evidence_used: Personal recollection of events and timing
escalation_path: Hotel front desk → Hyatt corporate customer service (advised)
cases.reusable_lesson: Safety-related complaints (fire alarm mismanagement) carry more weight than amenity complaints. Write to corporate customer service rather than the hotel directly for safety issues. Multiple consecutive alarms without communication is a genuine safety hazard worth escalating.
cases.notes: Guest was on a high floor (40+). Elevators were disabled during the alarm. The alarm was triggered by the rooftop bar.
review_notes: No reported resolution; useful only as an issue narrative, not an outcome datapoint.

cases.facts: Globalist guest staying at a Hyatt airport property. The guest's partner was in bed (naked) while the guest was out. A hotel employee entered the room without knocking or announcing — likely housekeeping who had not been informed of a late checkout request made by phone at 10am. The physical security latch was not engaged. Partner was distressed by the intrusion.
requested_compensation: Globalist customer care review of hotel procedures
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported. Forum was divided: some said to complain to corporate for the privacy breach, others noted the guest should have used the security latch and that late checkout communication failure was partially responsible.
evidence_used: Phone call log showing late checkout request time
cases.reusable_lesson: Always use the physical security latch when in the room, even for a moment. When requesting late checkout by phone, ask the front desk to note it in the system immediately. For serious privacy violations at a Hyatt, the Globalist email channel provides better documentation than phone calls.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Privacy/security issue. Outcome not reported.
review_notes: Privacy/safety incident with disputed facts and no reported outcome.

cases.facts: Guest arrived at a Reno Hyatt Place at 2am after highway delays (I-80). They had checked in via the app with a room number assigned, but the front desk gave a different room — a suite. The suite was actually intended for another guest with a similar name (mix-up). After correcting the error, the guest was given their actual room where the pillows had hair, the duvet had dog hair, and there was an eyelash on the sheets. The front desk phone was unreachable, so the guest had to go downstairs to request a room change. The hotel offered no upgrade or compensation — just a casual apology. The guest suspected the hotel had suites available but declined to upgrade them despite their Explorist status and explicit request.
requested_compensation: Compensation in points (guest was seeking advice)
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported in the captured thread. The guest was advised by ChatGPT and commenters to email management requesting points compensation.
evidence_used: Observations of dirty bedding (hair, dog hair, eyelash)
escalation_path: Front desk (in-person room change) → Hotel management email (advised)
cases.reusable_lesson: Hyatt Place properties are excluded from Globalist suite upgrade benefits. Document cleanliness issues with photos and contact hotel management directly rather than the front desk. Use AI to draft complaint emails.
cases.notes: Guest was an Explorist (水球 - low-tier). Hotel was full (peak season for Reno Air Races). The hotel mix-up revealed that suites were available but not offered.
review_notes: No reported resolution; useful only as an issue narrative, not an outcome datapoint.

cases.facts: Hotel experienced a power outage. The backup generator also failed, leaving no electricity, elevator, or大堂 services. Guest was unsure whether the hotel would relocate guests if power was not restored. Power was still out after 3 hours. Other forum users shared similar experiences: one had a Hyatt power outage in Bakersville, CA with no compensation beyond an apology despite being a Globalist.
requested_compensation: Relocation to a functioning hotel if power not restored
Points or refund for the unusable portion of the stay
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported. Forum shared experiences from other power outages where hotels provided apologies but minimal compensation.
cases.reusable_lesson: During a power outage, ask whether the hotel has a relocation policy for guests whose rooms are unusable. If the backup generator also fails, the room is effectively uninhabitable and the hotel should offer a solution. Points bookings may have different compensation than cash bookings.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Facts clear but outcome not reported.
review_notes: Outcome is incomplete; do not use as a compensation benchmark.

cases.facts: Guest staying at a Marriott Autograph Collection property in Nanjing during a flash promo. First night: leftover ketchup packet found torn open in a suspicious way. Hotel did pest control but did not change rooms. Second night: heard scratching sounds. Morning: found bite marks on bar soap. AI analysis suggested rats/mice. Guest changed rooms after reporting. Manager offered one bottle of wine + 5,000 points as compensation. Guest declined, considering 5,000 points insufficient for a pest issue. Manager noted that a full refund would forfeit the 4,000 flash promo bonus points per night ($400/night rate).
requested_compensation: More than 5,000 points for pest infestation
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome not reported. Guest was considering next steps and wanted advice on reasonable compensation amount.
evidence_used: Photo of bite marks on soap
cases.reusable_lesson: For pest-related hotel issues, provide clear photographic evidence and escalate to corporate customer care if the property's offer seems inadequate. Consider whether accepting a partial compensation (points) is better than a full refund that forfeits flash promo bonuses. Request written confirmation of any agreed compensation.
cases.notes: Summarized from USCardForum topic. Pest/sanitation issue at a Chinese Marriott property.
review_notes: Outcome is incomplete; do not use as a compensation benchmark.

cases.brand_or_airline: Hotel Figueroa (Unbound Collection) → The Hoxton, Downtown LA
cases.facts: Booked Hotel Figueroa for 20k points (cash rate $700+) at Hyatt. Hotel called ahead to say sold out, offered to move to The Hoxton, Downtown LA ($606/night cash rate) and refund points. OP was concerned about losing elite benefits (free parking, breakfast, late checkout). Negotiated before accepting.
cases.actual_outcome: 20k points refunded (full), 5k additional goodwill points, parking and breakfast differential refunded. Effectively free night at comparable hotel + 5k bonus points.
cases.reusable_lesson: When contacted before arrival, confirm the substitute hotel and treatment of points, parking, breakfast, and transport before accepting. The extra 5,000 points were this case's goodwill outcome, not a standard benchmark.
cases.notes: OP was proactive and negotiated before arrival. Outcome was positive.

cases.brand_or_airline: Hyatt Place Kyoto → Hyatt Regency Kyoto
cases.facts: Arrived at Hyatt Place Kyoto after mobile check-in, only to be told hotel was oversold. Walked to Hyatt Regency Kyoto with hotel covering taxi fare. OP had already mailed luggage to HP and had to buy replacement toiletries.
cases.actual_outcome: Taxi fare covered by hotel. Free drinks, 2pm late checkout, free breakfast at Regency. No additional points. Most forum members felt compensation was reasonable.
escalation_path: Hyatt concierge line (considered but not used)
cases.reusable_lesson: Mobile check-in does not guarantee a room. If walk involves moving to a different area, insist on luggage transfer assistance.
cases.notes: Limited compensation because walk was to a higher-category hotel. Japanese hotel practices differ from North America.

cases.facts: Booked two studios (17k points/night each) at Suncadia Resort. Hotel called before arrival offering to merge into 2BR suite for $100/night extra; OP refused. Upon arrival, hotel claimed no rooms available and offered a house in an annex building (no pool access, 10-min walk in 5°C weather). OP had called twice beforehand to confirm not being moved, but hotel denied knowledge. Negotiation lasted 15 minutes with OP recording video, insisting on original booking. Eventually hotel found two upgraded rooms in main building.
cases.actual_outcome: Both rooms were ultimately provided in the main lodge and the promised $500 dining credit was honored. A 68,000-point refund was discussed, but the source's final update said it apparently had not posted.
evidence_used: video recording of front desk conversation
cases.reusable_lesson: Confirm any relocation or room change before accepting it, and document the agreed room, credits, and refund separately. A verbal promise is not a completed points refund; follow up until each item is posted.
cases.notes: Source-checked: the rooms and dining credit were confirmed, but the initially promised 68,000-point refund was not confirmed in the final update.

cases.facts: Arrived at 11:30pm to a pre-booked Crowne Plaza. Front desk said 'we are overbooked' and security guard suggested checking a nearby motel. OP was Platinum Elite member. IHG has a Reservation Guarantee that should have provided alternate comparable accommodation. OP used ChatGPT to draft a complaint to IHG customer service.
requested_compensation: First-night lodging cost under the applicable reservation guarantee
cases.actual_outcome: Outcome was not reported in the captured source. Replies suggested escalating because the property had not arranged a comparable alternate hotel.
cases.reusable_lesson: For a qualifying direct reservation secured by credit card, compare the property's response with IHG's current Online Reservation Guarantee and ask the property or customer care to arrange the stated alternate lodging and transport.
cases.notes: The source documents the walk but no final resolution. The earlier 15,000-point outcome was unsupported and has been removed.
review_notes: The captured source does not report the claimed 15,000-point outcome.

cases.facts: Booked Holiday Inn Springfield for 2 nights (17k + 22k points). Arrived 10:30pm, told hotel was full. Handwritten note sent to adjacent Crown Plaza. Crown Plaza hadn't been notified. No bottled water provided despite 3 requests. OP later discovered IHG had refunded all points.
cases.actual_outcome: Full points refunded (39k points) - both nights comped. No additional compensation.
evidence_used: handwritten note from Holiday Inn front desk
cases.reusable_lesson: Verify that the receiving hotel has the relocation details and check whether points were returned. The source reports a full points refund, while IHG's current Online Reservation Guarantee separately describes alternate lodging and transportation for eligible reservations.
cases.notes: Full points refund without even asking. Walk was handled poorly (handwritten note, no notification to receiving hotel).

cases.facts: Guest had a confirmed direct booking with Bonvoy number attached. At check-in, the hotel said it was oversold and moved the guest to a nearby lower-tier property.
cases.actual_outcome: Demo example: hotel covered relocation and added points after escalation.
cases.reusable_lesson: Emphasize confirmed reservation, Bonvoy number attached, and ask for the Ultimate Reservation Guarantee to be applied in writing.
cases.notes: Synthetic example for demo only. Replace with real summarized DP before public launch.

scripts.template: Please confirm whether my booking and membership meet Marriott's Ultimate Reservation Guarantee conditions. Please explain available nearby accommodation, transport support and any applicable guarantee remedy in writing.
scripts.when_to_use: Use at the front desk when a Marriott property says it cannot honor a confirmed reservation.

scripts.template: Please review my reported reservation problem, confirm the booking status, and explain available alternate accommodation and transport support. Please identify the evidence needed to review any documented expenses or applicable guarantee. Additional goodwill is a separate discretionary request.
scripts.when_to_use: Use after a hotel walk when the property did not fully resolve relocation or documented expenses.
